title: Provider-neutral Task and Follow-up Agent can create only a matched ordinary task

given.provider: one explicit test-only task_follow_up fake/spy executor; production remains unbound and fail closed
given.context: strict PostgreSQL task, outcome, and evidence records only
given.run_identity: one injected TaskFollowUp command run_id; no durable worker/scheduler delivery identity exists

when.success_flow: typed model proposal passes the post-model current guard, becomes one transient pending task_request envelope, receives the matching project classification, and reaches the canonical ordinary Task writer
when.denial_flow: the same stage instead observes archive or revoke and returns a blocked result before any envelope, classification, or Task write

then.same_run_retry: a repeated internal invocation may repeat model, audit, and classifier work because no durable runtime replay contract exists; canonical ordinary-dispatch run/message uniqueness and Task request idempotency still prevent a second Task
then.consumed_retry: the classified disposition and Task unique classification link preserve write-side one-shot idempotency; an exact classified retry repeats current ActorContext/Farm/Plant read authority and returns the existing Task without another Task write
then.restore_and_concurrency: a pre-classification denial is re-evaluated under current authority if explicitly invoked again; real concurrent classified writers serialize and commit at most one consumed-or-denied disposition and one Task, while runtime-ledger crash windows and zero-call replay are not current acceptance
then.action_trigger_policy: an action trigger allows only check|measurement because action completion exclusively owns its deterministic +48-hour follow_up; completion during provider I/O or after the invocation cannot leave a second ordinary follow_up
